κμ=nsnall,\kappa_{\mu}=\frac{n_{s}}{n_{\mathrm{all}}},

and

κμn0≤nsn0​nall,κμns≤nsn0​nall.\frac{\kappa_{\mu}}{\sqrt{n_{0}}}\leq\sqrt{\frac{n_{s}}{n_{0}n_{\mathrm{all}}}},\qquad\frac{\kappa_{\mu}}{\sqrt{n_{s}}}\leq\sqrt{\frac{n_{s}}{n_{0}n_{\mathrm{all}}}}.

Therefore,

‖ζτ,e‖∞=Op​(ns​log⁡(q∨2)n0​nall).\left\|\zeta_{\tau,e}\right\|_{\infty}=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{\frac{n_{s}\log(q\vee 2)}{n_{0}n_{\mathrm{all}}}}\right).

For q≥2q\geq 2 and any fixed A>0A>0, the coordinate tail bound above and a union bound over tasks, coordinates, and the fixed number of iterations show that, outside an event of probability at most 2​Υ​(K+1)​q1−c​A2+o⁡(1)2\Upsilon(K+1)q^{1-cA^{2}}+o(1),

‖gτ,e(k)‖∞≤A​log⁡qnk,0≤k≤K,1≤τ≤Υ.\left\|g_{\tau,e}^{(k)}\right\|_{\infty}\leq A\sqrt{\frac{\log q}{n_{k}}},\qquad 0\leq k\leq K,\quad 1\leq\tau\leq\Upsilon.

On the intersection of the event where the preceding bound holds and the profile-stability event,

maxτ≤Υ⁡‖ζτ,e‖∞\displaystyle\max_{\tau\leq\Upsilon}\left\|\zeta_{\tau,e}\right\|_{\infty} ≤A​Cprof​κμ​log⁡q​(1n0+Cprof​∑k=1Kwknk)\displaystyle\leq AC_{\mathrm{prof}}\kappa_{\mu}\sqrt{\log q}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_{0}}}+C_{\mathrm{prof}}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{w_{k}}{\sqrt{n_{k}}}\right)
≤A​Cprof​(1+Cprof​K)​ns​log⁡qn0​nall.\displaystyle\leq AC_{\mathrm{prof}}(1+C_{\mathrm{prof}}\sqrt{K})\sqrt{\frac{n_{s}\log q}{n_{0}n_{\mathrm{all}}}}.

Choose AA so that c​A2>1cA^{2}>1 and then choose cΔ≥2​A​Cprof​(1+Cprof​K)c_{\Delta}\geq 2AC_{\mathrm{prof}}(1+C_{\mathrm{prof}}\sqrt{K}). Since

λΔ=cΔ​ns​log⁡qn0​nall,\lambda_{\Delta}=c_{\Delta}\sqrt{\frac{n_{s}\log q}{n_{0}n_{\mathrm{all}}}},

it follows that

ℙ⁡(maxτ≤Υ⁡‖ζτ,e‖∞>λΔ2)≤2​Υ​(K+1)​q1−c​A2+o⁡(1),\mathbb{P}\left(\max_{\tau\leq\Upsilon}\left\|\zeta_{\tau,e}\right\|_{\infty}>\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{2}\right)\leq 2\Upsilon(K+1)q^{1-cA^{2}}+o(1),

which tends to zero when q→∞q\to\infty. ∎

One-step coefficient error.

We combine the profile identities and score bounds with the sieve remainder to obtain the one-step coefficient error below.

Lemma \thechapter.A.2 (One-step target coefficient error).

Suppose the sample-splitting, sieve-approximation, low-complexity correction, and profile-stability conditions hold, together with the conditions of Lemma 5.1. Let

μ=nsn0,λΔ=cΔ​ns​log⁡qn0​nall,\mu=\frac{n_{s}}{n_{0}},\qquad\lambda_{\Delta}=c_{\Delta}\sqrt{\frac{n_{s}\log q}{n_{0}n_{\mathrm{all}}}},

where cΔ>0c_{\Delta}>0 is sufficiently large, and define

λ¯Δ=λΔκμ,κμ=μ1+μ.\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}=\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{\kappa_{\mu}},\qquad\kappa_{\mu}=\frac{\mu}{1+\mu}.

Then, uniformly over τ=1,…,Υ\tau=1,\ldots,\Upsilon,

‖δ^τ−δτ,Δ(0)‖2=Op(Δs,hΔ+p−κ/d),\left\|\widehat{\delta}_{\tau}-\delta_{\tau,\Delta}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\Delta_{s,h_{\Delta}}+p^{-\kappa/d}\right),

where

Δs,hΔ=s​λ¯Δ∧hΔ​λ¯Δ∧hΔ.\Delta_{s,h_{\Delta}}=\sqrt{s}\,\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}\wedge\sqrt{h_{\Delta}\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}}\wedge h_{\Delta}.

Moreover,

‖β^τ(0)−βτ(0)‖2=Op(qnall+Δs,hΔ+p−κ/d).\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{\mathrm{all}}}}+\Delta_{s,h_{\Delta}}+p^{-\kappa/d}\right).
Proof of Lemma \thechapter.A.2.

Fix an iteration τ\tau and condition on the previous fitted iterates. Use the notation of the direct profiling calculation, and write ap=p−κ/da_{p}=p^{-\kappa/d}.

Step 1: Profile curvature and sieve approximation.

By Lemma 5.1, ℙ⁡(ℰΣ,τ)⟶1\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{\Sigma,\tau})\longrightarrow 1. On this event, the empirical Gram matrices and Ω^τ,s\widehat{\Omega}_{\tau,s} have eigenvalues bounded above and below. The variational identity (\thechapter.A.8) consequently gives

cM​κμ​‖h‖22≤h⊤​Mτ​h≤CM​κμ​‖h‖22,κμ=μ1+μ,c_{M}\kappa_{\mu}\|h\|_{2}^{2}\leq h^{\top}M_{\tau}h\leq C_{M}\kappa_{\mu}\|h\|_{2}^{2},\qquad\kappa_{\mu}=\frac{\mu}{1+\mu},

for constants 0<cM<CM<∞0<c_{M}<C_{M}<\infty.

For the approximation scores in (\thechapter.A.3), for every v∈ℝqv\in\mathbb{R}^{q} with ‖v‖2=1\|v\|_{2}=1,

v⊤Aτ,k−1/2gτ,r(k)\displaystyle v^{\top}A_{\tau,k}^{-1/2}g_{\tau,r}^{(k)} =1nk(Zτ(k)Aτ,k−1/2v)⊤rτ(k)\displaystyle=\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(k)}A_{\tau,k}^{-1/2}v\right)^{\top}r_{\tau}^{(k)}
≤[1nk‖Zτ(k)Aτ,k−1/2v‖22]1/2‖rτ(k)‖2nk\displaystyle\leq\left[\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left\|Z_{\tau}^{(k)}A_{\tau,k}^{-1/2}v\right\|_{2}^{2}\right]^{1/2}\frac{\|r_{\tau}^{(k)}\|_{2}}{\sqrt{n_{k}}}
≲ap.\displaystyle\lesssim a_{p}.

Consequently,

‖gτ,r(k)‖2≲ap.\left\|g_{\tau,r}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}\lesssim a_{p}.

The empirical-Gram bounds imply

‖sτ,r‖2≲ap.\|s_{\tau,r}\|_{2}\lesssim a_{p}.

For the approximation-score identity in (\thechapter.A.6), note that

I−Aτ,0​H^τ−1=μ​Ω^τ,s​H^τ−1,I-A_{\tau,0}\widehat{H}_{\tau}^{-1}=\mu\widehat{\Omega}_{\tau,s}\widehat{H}_{\tau}^{-1},

and

‖H^τ−1‖op≲11+μ.\left\|\widehat{H}_{\tau}^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\frac{1}{1+\mu}.

It follows that

‖ζτ,r‖2≲κμ​ap,\left\|\zeta_{\tau,r}\right\|_{2}\lesssim\kappa_{\mu}a_{p},

and hence

|ζτ,r⊤​h|≲κμ​ap​‖h‖2.\left|\zeta_{\tau,r}^{\top}h\right|\lesssim\kappa_{\mu}a_{p}\|h\|_{2}.

Step 2: Basic inequality.

By (\thechapter.A.2) and (\thechapter.A.7), the optimality of δ^τ\widehat{\delta}_{\tau} gives

12​h^τ⊤​Mτ​h^τ≤\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\widehat{h}_{\tau}^{\top}M_{\tau}\widehat{h}_{\tau}\leq{} ζτ,e⊤​h^τ+ζτ,r⊤​h^τ\displaystyle\zeta_{\tau,e}^{\top}\widehat{h}_{\tau}+\zeta_{\tau,r}^{\top}\widehat{h}_{\tau}
+λΔ​(‖δτ∗‖1−‖δτ∗+h^τ‖1).\displaystyle+\lambda_{\Delta}\left(\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}\|_{1}-\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}+\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\right).

We first treat q→∞q\to\infty, using the stochastic-score event from Lemma \thechapter.A.1,

‖ζτ,e‖∞≤λΔ2.\left\|\zeta_{\tau,e}\right\|_{\infty}\leq\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{2}.

Combining this event with the bounds from Step 1 yields

c​κμ​‖h^τ‖22≤\displaystyle c\kappa_{\mu}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}^{2}\leq{} λΔ2​‖h^τ‖1+λΔ​(‖δτ∗‖1−‖δτ∗+h^τ‖1)\displaystyle\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{2}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}+\lambda_{\Delta}\left(\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}\|_{1}-\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}+\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\right) (\thechapter.A.10)
+C​κμ​ap​‖h^τ‖2.\displaystyle+C\kappa_{\mu}a_{p}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}.

If ‖h^τ‖2≤C0​ap\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}\leq C_{0}a_{p} for a sufficiently large constant C0C_{0}, the desired approximation bound already holds. Otherwise, the final term in (\thechapter.A.10) can be absorbed into its left-hand side. Thus it remains to analyze

c​κμ​‖h^τ‖22≤λΔ2​‖h^τ‖1+λΔ​(‖δτ∗‖1−‖δτ∗+h^τ‖1).c\kappa_{\mu}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{2}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}+\lambda_{\Delta}\left(\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}\|_{1}-\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}+\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\right). (\thechapter.A.11)

Step 3: Adaptive discrepancy bounds.

Let

Sτ=supp⁡(δτ∗).S_{\tau}=\operatorname{supp}(\delta_{\tau}^{*}).

Since δτ,Sτc∗=0\delta_{\tau,S_{\tau}^{c}}^{*}=0,

‖δτ∗‖1−‖δτ∗+h^τ‖1≤‖h^τ,Sτ‖1−‖h^τ,Sτc‖1.\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}\|_{1}-\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}+\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\leq\|\widehat{h}_{\tau,S_{\tau}}\|_{1}-\|\widehat{h}_{\tau,S_{\tau}^{c}}\|_{1}.

Substituting this inequality into (\thechapter.A.11) and dropping the nonpositive term gives

c​κμ​‖h^τ‖22≤3​λΔ2​‖h^τ,Sτ‖1≤3​λΔ2​s​‖h^τ‖2.c\kappa_{\mu}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\frac{3\lambda_{\Delta}}{2}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau,S_{\tau}}\|_{1}\leq\frac{3\lambda_{\Delta}}{2}\sqrt{s}\,\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}.

Therefore,

‖h^τ‖2≲s​λΔκμ.\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}\lesssim\sqrt{s}\,\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{\kappa_{\mu}}. (\thechapter.A.12)

Alternatively, the reverse triangle inequality and ‖δτ∗‖1≤hΔ\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}\|_{1}\leq h_{\Delta} imply

‖δτ∗‖1−‖δτ∗+h^τ‖1≤2​hΔ−‖h^τ‖1.\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}\|_{1}-\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}+\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\leq 2h_{\Delta}-\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}.

Using this inequality in (\thechapter.A.11) and dropping the resulting nonpositive ℓ1\ell_{1} term gives

c​κμ​‖h^τ‖22≤2​λΔ​hΔ,c\kappa_{\mu}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}^{2}\leq 2\lambda_{\Delta}h_{\Delta},

and hence

‖h^τ‖2≲hΔ​λΔκμ.\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}\lesssim\sqrt{h_{\Delta}\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{\kappa_{\mu}}}. (\thechapter.A.13)

If instead we retain the negative term, then

c​κμ​‖h^τ‖22+λΔ2​‖h^τ‖1≤2​λΔ​hΔ.c\kappa_{\mu}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}^{2}+\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{2}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\leq 2\lambda_{\Delta}h_{\Delta}.

Dropping the quadratic term yields

‖h^τ‖2≤‖h^τ‖1≲hΔ.\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}\leq\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\lesssim h_{\Delta}. (\thechapter.A.14)

Combining (\thechapter.A.12)–(\thechapter.A.14) with the case ‖h^τ‖2≲ap\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}\lesssim a_{p} gives

‖δ^τ−δτ∗‖2=Op​(s​λ¯Δ∧hΔ​λ¯Δ∧hΔ+ap),\left\|\widehat{\delta}_{\tau}-\delta_{\tau}^{*}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{s}\,\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}\wedge\sqrt{h_{\Delta}\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}}\wedge h_{\Delta}+a_{p}\right),

where

λ¯Δ=λΔκμ.\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}=\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{\kappa_{\mu}}.

Equivalently,

‖δ^τ−δτ∗‖2=Op(Δs,hΔ+p−κ/d).\left\|\widehat{\delta}_{\tau}-\delta_{\tau}^{*}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\Delta_{s,h_{\Delta}}+p^{-\kappa/d}\right). (\thechapter.A.15)

Step 4: Reconstruction of the target coefficient.

The exact identity (\thechapter.A.9) separates the pooled score contribution from the correction contribution. By the empirical-Gram bounds,

‖H^τ−1‖op≲11+μ.\left\|\widehat{H}_{\tau}^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\frac{1}{1+\mu}.

Together with the Euclidean score bounds in Lemma \thechapter.A.1, this gives

‖H^τ−1​[gτ,e(0)+μ​sτ,e]‖2\displaystyle\left\|\widehat{H}_{\tau}^{-1}\left[g_{\tau,e}^{(0)}+\mu s_{\tau,e}\right]\right\|_{2} =Op​[11+μ​(qn0+μ​qns)]\displaystyle=O_{p}\left[\frac{1}{1+\mu}\left(\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{0}}}+\mu\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{s}}}\right)\right] (\thechapter.A.16)
=Op​(qnall),\displaystyle=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{\mathrm{all}}}}\right),

where the last equality uses μ=ns/n0\mu=n_{s}/n_{0}.

The approximation-score bounds from Step 1 similarly imply

‖H^τ−1​[gτ,r(0)+μ​sτ,r]‖2≲ap.\left\|\widehat{H}_{\tau}^{-1}\left[g_{\tau,r}^{(0)}+\mu s_{\tau,r}\right]\right\|_{2}\lesssim a_{p}. (\thechapter.A.17)

Finally,

‖μ​H^τ−1​Ω^τ,s‖op≲1.\left\|\mu\widehat{H}_{\tau}^{-1}\widehat{\Omega}_{\tau,s}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim 1. (\thechapter.A.18)

Combining (\thechapter.A.15), (\thechapter.A.9), and the preceding stochastic, approximation, and correction-map bounds yields

‖β^τ(0)−βτ(0)‖2=Op(qnall+Δs,hΔ+p−κ/d).\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{\mathrm{all}}}}+\Delta_{s,h_{\Delta}}+p^{-\kappa/d}\right).

Probability bookkeeping.

If qq is bounded, the optimality inequality in Step 2, Step 1, and ‖δτ∗‖1−‖δτ∗+h^τ‖1≤q​‖h^τ‖2\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}\|_{1}-\|\delta_{\tau}^{*}+\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{1}\leq\sqrt{q}\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2} give

‖h^τ‖2≲ap+qκμ​(‖ζτ,e‖∞+λΔ).\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}\lesssim a_{p}+\frac{\sqrt{q}}{\kappa_{\mu}}\left(\|\zeta_{\tau,e}\|_{\infty}+\lambda_{\Delta}\right).

By Lemma \thechapter.A.1 and the definition of λΔ\lambda_{\Delta}, the second term is op​(1)o_{p}(1) for bounded qq, since nmin→∞n_{\min}\to\infty. As q=m​pq=mp is bounded, ap=p−κ/da_{p}=p^{-\kappa/d} is bounded below, so ‖h^τ‖2=Op​(ap)\|\widehat{h}_{\tau}\|_{2}=O_{p}(a_{p}) in this case.

Thus (\thechapter.A.15) also holds for bounded qq, and the same reconstruction bounds in Step 4 give the target coefficient bound. The preceding argument proves (\thechapter.A.15) when q→∞q\to\infty; the bounded-qq argument above proves it when qq remains bounded. The same bound holds for sequences on which qq does not converge: split at a fixed q0q_{0}. The bounded-qq argument applies for q<q0q<q_{0}, while for q≥q0q\geq q_{0} the score-event failure probability is at most 2​Υ​(K+1)​q01−c​A2+o⁡(1)2\Upsilon(K+1)q_{0}^{1-cA^{2}}+o(1), which can be made arbitrarily small by increasing q0q_{0}.

The reconstruction bounds apply to both parts of this split. Since the number of FQI iterations is fixed, the conclusion holds uniformly over τ=1,…,Υ\tau=1,\ldots,\Upsilon by a finite union bound. This completes the proof. ∎

Proof of Theorem 5.1.

Proof.

Step 1: From coefficient error to the Bellman residual.

Write

𝔯n=p−κ/d+q/nall+Δs,hΔ.\mathfrak{r}_{n}=p^{-\kappa/d}+\sqrt{q/n_{\mathrm{all}}}+\Delta_{s,h_{\Delta}}.

Lemma \thechapter.A.2 gives

‖β^τ(0)−βτ(0)‖2=Op​(𝔯n),\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}(\mathfrak{r}_{n}),

uniformly over τ=1,…,Υ\tau=1,\ldots,\Upsilon. We translate this bound into control of the target Bellman residual.

Let 𝔇0\mathfrak{D}_{0} denote the collection of state-action distributions generated from the target initial distribution ν(0)\nu^{(0)} by arbitrary finite sequences of target-task Markov policies, allowing arbitrary current-action choices at the final state, together with their countable convex mixtures, including discounted occupancy distributions. For a measurable function gg, write

‖g‖L1​(ν)=𝔼ν​[|g⁡(X,A)|],ν∈𝔇0.\|g\|_{L_{1}(\nu)}=\mathbb{E}_{\nu}[|g(X,A)|],\qquad\nu\in\mathfrak{D}_{0}.

These integrals are evaluated with the fitted functions held fixed.

By Assumption 5.1(iii), the target initial-state density is uniformly bounded. Moreover, under the standard definition of the Hölder ball, Assumption 5.2(i) implies that the transition density is uniformly bounded. Hence, the state marginal of every distribution in 𝔇0\mathfrak{D}_{0} has a uniformly bounded density. In addition, Lemma E.1 of the supplementary material to Shi et al. (2022a) gives the following standard property for B-spline and wavelet bases:

λmax​(∫𝒳ϕ⁡(x)​ϕ⊤​(x)​𝑑x)≲1.\lambda_{\max}\left(\int_{\mathcal{X}}\phi(x)\phi^{\top}(x)\,dx\right)\lesssim 1.

It follows that, uniformly over ν∈𝔇0\nu\in\mathfrak{D}_{0},

𝔼ν​[{ξ⊤​(X,A)​u}2]≲‖u‖22,u∈ℝq.\mathbb{E}_{\nu}\big[\{\xi^{\top}(X,A)u\}^{2}\big]\lesssim\|u\|_{2}^{2},\qquad u\in\mathbb{R}^{q}. (\thechapter.A.19)

Indeed, writing u=(u1⊤,…,um⊤)⊤u=(u_{1}^{\top},\ldots,u_{m}^{\top})^{\top} with ua∈ℝpu_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}, the left-hand side of (\thechapter.A.19) is bounded by a constant multiple of

∑a=1mua⊤​(∫𝒳ϕ⁡(x)​ϕ⊤​(x)​𝑑x)​ua≲∑a=1m‖ua‖22=‖u‖22.\sum_{a=1}^{m}u_{a}^{\top}\left(\int_{\mathcal{X}}\phi(x)\phi^{\top}(x)\,dx\right)u_{a}\lesssim\sum_{a=1}^{m}\|u_{a}\|_{2}^{2}=\|u\|_{2}^{2}.

For iteration τ\tau, define the target Bellman residual

dτ=𝒯(0)​Q^τ−1(0)−Q^τ(0).d_{\tau}=\mathcal{T}^{(0)}\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(0)}-\widehat{Q}_{\tau}^{(0)}.

Since fτ(0)=𝒯(0)​Q^τ−1(0)f_{\tau}^{(0)}=\mathcal{T}^{(0)}\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(0)} and Q^τ(0)​(x,a)=ξ⊤​(x,a)​β^τ(0)\widehat{Q}_{\tau}^{(0)}(x,a)=\xi^{\top}(x,a)\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)},

dτ​(x,a)=fτ(0)​(x,a)−ξ⊤​(x,a)​βτ(0)+ξ⊤​(x,a)​{βτ(0)−β^τ(0)}.\begin{split}d_{\tau}(x,a)={}&f_{\tau}^{(0)}(x,a)-\xi^{\top}(x,a)\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\\ &+\xi^{\top}(x,a)\{\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}-\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}\}.\end{split}

Consequently, the sieve approximation bound, (\thechapter.A.19), and Cauchy–Schwarz imply

supν∈𝔇0‖dτ‖L1​(ν)≲p−κ/d+∥β^τ(0)−βτ(0)∥2=Op​(𝔯n),\begin{split}\sup_{\nu\in\mathfrak{D}_{0}}\|d_{\tau}\|_{L_{1}(\nu)}&\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d}+\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\|_{2}\\ &=O_{p}(\mathfrak{r}_{n}),\end{split} (\thechapter.A.20)

uniformly over τ=1,…,Υ\tau=1,\ldots,\Upsilon.

Step 2: FQI error propagation and initialization.

Write Q∗=Q∗,(0)Q^{*}=Q^{*,(0)}. For any policy ω\omega and measurable function g:𝒳×𝒜→ℝg:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{R}, define

(Pωg)(x,a)=𝔼[g(X′,A′)∣X′∼P(⋅∣x,a),A′∼ω(⋅∣X′)].(P^{\omega}g)(x,a)=\mathbb{E}\big[g(X^{\prime},A^{\prime})\mid X^{\prime}\sim P(\cdot\mid x,a),\ A^{\prime}\sim\omega(\cdot\mid X^{\prime})\big].

The reward bound and the assumed initialization give

‖Q∗−Q^0(0)‖∞≤‖Q∗‖∞+‖Q^0(0)‖∞≤2​Rmax1−γ.\|Q^{*}-\widehat{Q}_{0}^{(0)}\|_{\infty}\leq\|Q^{*}\|_{\infty}+\|\widehat{Q}_{0}^{(0)}\|_{\infty}\leq\frac{2R_{\max}}{1-\gamma}.

Each PωP^{\omega} preserves uniform bounds. Following the error-propagation argument in Lemma C.2 of Fan et al. (2020), and taking absolute values and suprema over Markov policy sequences, we therefore obtain

|Q∗​(x,a)−Q^Υ(0)​(x,a)|≤∑τ=1ΥγΥ−τsupω1,…,ωΥ−τ(PωΥ−τ⋯Pω1|dτ|)(x,a)+2​γΥ​Rmax1−γ.\begin{split}|Q^{*}(x,a)-\widehat{Q}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}(x,a)|\leq{}&\sum_{\tau=1}^{\Upsilon}\gamma^{\Upsilon-\tau}\sup_{\omega_{1},\ldots,\omega_{\Upsilon-\tau}}\big(P^{\omega_{\Upsilon-\tau}}\cdots P^{\omega_{1}}|d_{\tau}|\big)(x,a)\\ &+\frac{2\gamma^{\Upsilon}R_{\max}}{1-\gamma}.\end{split} (\thechapter.A.21)

Here a product of zero transition operators is the identity, and the supremum over an empty policy sequence leaves |dΥ||d_{\Upsilon}| unchanged.

For a nonnegative terminal function, backward maximization over the finite action set, with a fixed tie-breaking rule, constructs measurable Markov policies attaining each pointwise supremum in (\thechapter.A.21). Appending such a policy sequence preserves 𝔇0\mathfrak{D}_{0}. Thus, integrating each propagated residual against any ν∈𝔇0\nu\in\mathfrak{D}_{0} is bounded by supν′∈𝔇0‖dτ‖L1​(ν′)\sup_{\nu^{\prime}\in\mathfrak{D}_{0}}\|d_{\tau}\|_{L_{1}(\nu^{\prime})}. Using (\thechapter.A.20) and summing the geometric series gives

supν∈𝔇0‖Q∗−Q^Υ(0)‖L1​(ν)≤Op​(𝔯n​∑j=0Υ−1γj)+2​γΥ​Rmax1−γ=Op​(𝔯n1−γ+γΥ​Rmax1−γ).\begin{split}\sup_{\nu\in\mathfrak{D}_{0}}\|Q^{*}-\widehat{Q}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}\|_{L_{1}(\nu)}&\leq O_{p}\left(\mathfrak{r}_{n}\sum_{j=0}^{\Upsilon-1}\gamma^{j}\right)+\frac{2\gamma^{\Upsilon}R_{\max}}{1-\gamma}\\ &=O_{p}\left(\frac{\mathfrak{r}_{n}}{1-\gamma}+\frac{\gamma^{\Upsilon}R_{\max}}{1-\gamma}\right).\end{split} (\thechapter.A.22)

Step 3: From the greedy policy to value loss.

Let

π^Υ(0)​(x)∈arg⁡maxa∈𝒜​Q^Υ(0)​(x,a).\widehat{\pi}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}(x)\in\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\widehat{Q}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}(x,a).

The greedy property implies, for every xx,

Q∗​(x,π∗,(0)​(x))−Q∗​(x,π^Υ(0)​(x))≤|Q∗−Q^Υ(0)​|(x,π∗,(0)​(x))+|​Q∗−Q^Υ(0)|(x,π^Υ(0)​(x)).\begin{split}&Q^{*}\big(x,\pi^{*,(0)}(x)\big)-Q^{*}\big(x,\widehat{\pi}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}(x)\big)\\ &\quad\leq\big|Q^{*}-\widehat{Q}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}\big|\big(x,\pi^{*,(0)}(x)\big)+\big|Q^{*}-\widehat{Q}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}\big|\big(x,\widehat{\pi}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}(x)\big).\end{split}

The normalized discounted state occupancy of the learned policy is a countable mixture of reachable state distributions. Its current-action lifts under π∗,(0)\pi^{*,(0)} and π^Υ(0)\widehat{\pi}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)} both belong to 𝔇0\mathfrak{D}_{0}. Applying the standard performance-difference argument under this occupancy, and then (\thechapter.A.22), yields

vπ∗,(0),(0)−vπ^Υ(0),(0)≤21−γ​supν∈𝔇0‖Q∗−Q^Υ(0)‖L1​(ν)=Op​(𝔯n(1−γ)2+γΥ​Rmax(1−γ)2)=1(1−γ)2Op(p−κ/d+q/nall+Δs,hΔ+γΥRmax).\begin{split}v^{\pi^{*,(0)},(0)}-v^{\widehat{\pi}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)},(0)}&\leq\frac{2}{1-\gamma}\sup_{\nu\in\mathfrak{D}_{0}}\|Q^{*}-\widehat{Q}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}\|_{L_{1}(\nu)}\\ &=O_{p}\left(\frac{\mathfrak{r}_{n}}{(1-\gamma)^{2}}+\frac{\gamma^{\Upsilon}R_{\max}}{(1-\gamma)^{2}}\right)\\ &=\frac{1}{(1-\gamma)^{2}}O_{p}\left(p^{-\kappa/d}+\sqrt{q/n_{\mathrm{all}}}+\Delta_{s,h_{\Delta}}+\gamma^{\Upsilon}R_{\max}\right).\end{split}

This establishes the stated value-loss bound and completes the proof of Theorem 5.1. ∎

Proof of Theorem 5.2

We now consider the transition-heterogeneous setting. The reward functions, behavior policies, initial-state distributions, and population sieve design matrices may vary across tasks, as in the transition-homogeneous setting. Here, the transition kernels P(k)P^{(k)} may vary as well.

For each task k∈{0}∪[K]k\in\{0\}\cup[K], define its Bellman optimality operator by

(𝒯(k)​Q)​(x,a)=r(k)​(x,a)+γ​∫𝒳maxa′∈𝒜⁡Q⁡(x′,a′)​ρ(k)​(x′∣x,a)​d​x′.\left(\mathcal{T}^{(k)}Q\right)(x,a)=r^{(k)}(x,a)+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{X}}\max_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}}Q(x^{\prime},a^{\prime})\rho^{(k)}(x^{\prime}\mid x,a)\,dx^{\prime}.

For a target-task policy ω\omega, define

(P(0),ωg)(x,a)=𝔼[g(X′,A′)∣X′∼P(0)(⋅∣x,a),A′∼ω(⋅∣X′)].\left(P^{(0),\omega}g\right)(x,a)=\mathbb{E}\left[g(X^{\prime},A^{\prime})\mid X^{\prime}\sim P^{(0)}(\cdot\mid x,a),\;A^{\prime}\sim\omega(\cdot\mid X^{\prime})\right].

Allowing source transition kernels to differ from the target kernel does not change the FQI error-propagation argument for the target estimator. This argument involves only the target Bellman operator 𝒯(0)\mathcal{T}^{(0)} and the target transition kernel P(0)P^{(0)}. Therefore, with the convention that a product of zero transition operators is the identity operator,

|Q∗,(0)−Q^Υ(0)|≤\displaystyle\left|Q^{*,(0)}-\widehat{Q}_{\Upsilon}^{(0)}\right|\leq{} ∑τ=0Υ−1γΥ−1−τsupω1,…,ωΥ−1−τ(P(0),ωΥ−1−τ⋯P(0),ω1)\displaystyle\sum_{\tau=0}^{\Upsilon-1}\gamma^{\Upsilon-1-\tau}\sup_{\omega_{1},\ldots,\omega_{\Upsilon-1-\tau}}\left(P^{(0),\omega_{\Upsilon-1-\tau}}\cdots P^{(0),\omega_{1}}\right) (\thechapter.A.23)
|𝒯(0)​Q^τ(0)−Q^τ+1(0)|+2​γΥ​Rmax1−γ.\displaystyle\left|\mathcal{T}^{(0)}\widehat{Q}_{\tau}^{(0)}-\widehat{Q}_{\tau+1}^{(0)}\right|+\frac{2\gamma^{\Upsilon}R_{\max}}{1-\gamma}.

Consequently, it suffices to control the one-step target Bellman residual

|𝒯(0)​Q^τ−1(0)−Q^τ(0)|\left|\mathcal{T}^{(0)}\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(0)}-\widehat{Q}_{\tau}^{(0)}\right|

uniformly over τ=1,…,Υ\tau=1,\ldots,\Upsilon.

Fix an iteration τ\tau, and let ℱτ−1\mathcal{F}_{\tau-1} be the sigma-field generated by the initial fitted functions and the data blocks 𝒟1,…,𝒟τ−1\mathcal{D}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{D}_{\tau-1}. The round block 𝒟τ\mathcal{D}_{\tau} is independent of ℱτ−1\mathcal{F}_{\tau-1}.

For every task k∈{0}∪[K]k\in\{0\}\cup[K], the pseudo-response is

Yi,t(k),τ=Ri,t(k)+γ​maxa′∈𝒜​Q^τ−1(k)​(Xi,t+1(k),a′),(i,t)∈Sτ(k).Y_{i,t}^{(k),\tau}=R_{i,t}^{(k)}+\gamma\max_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}}\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}\left(X_{i,t+1}^{(k)},a^{\prime}\right),\qquad(i,t)\in S_{\tau}^{(k)}.

Its conditional expectation is

𝔼[Yi,t(k),τ∣Xi,t(k),Ai,t(k),ℱτ−1]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[Y_{i,t}^{(k),\tau}\mid X_{i,t}^{(k)},A_{i,t}^{(k)},\mathcal{F}_{\tau-1}\right]
=(𝒯(k)​Q^τ−1(k))​(Xi,t(k),Ai,t(k)).\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{T}^{(k)}\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}\right)\left(X_{i,t}^{(k)},A_{i,t}^{(k)}\right).

Define the task-specific population Bellman regression function

fτ(k)=𝒯(k)​Q^τ−1(k).f_{\tau}^{(k)}=\mathcal{T}^{(k)}\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}.

Then

Yi,t(k),τ=fτ(k)​(Xi,t(k),Ai,t(k))+ei,t(k),τ,Y_{i,t}^{(k),\tau}=f_{\tau}^{(k)}\left(X_{i,t}^{(k)},A_{i,t}^{(k)}\right)+e_{i,t}^{(k),\tau},

where

𝔼[ei,t(k),τ∣Xi,t(k),Ai,t(k),ℱτ−1]=0.\mathbb{E}\left[e_{i,t}^{(k),\tau}\mid X_{i,t}^{(k)},A_{i,t}^{(k)},\mathcal{F}_{\tau-1}\right]=0.

Under the reward-noise condition and the uniform boundedness of the previous fitted iterates, ei,t(k),τe_{i,t}^{(k),\tau} is conditionally sub-Gaussian.

By the approximation property in Assumption 5.2(i), the coefficients defined above for each task kk, namely

βr(k)∈ℝq\beta_{r}^{(k)}\in\mathbb{R}^{q}

and

{βρ(k)​(x′)∈ℝq:x′∈𝒳}\left\{\beta_{\rho}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\in\mathbb{R}^{q}:x^{\prime}\in\mathcal{X}\right\}

satisfy

supx,a,k|r(k)(x,a)−ξ⊤(x,a)βr(k)|≲p−κ/d,\sup_{x,a,k}\left|r^{(k)}(x,a)-\xi^{\top}(x,a)\beta_{r}^{(k)}\right|\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d},

and

supx,a,x′,k|ρ(k)(x′∣x,a)−ξ⊤(x,a)βρ(k)(x′)|≲p−κ/d.\sup_{x,a,x^{\prime},k}\left|\rho^{(k)}(x^{\prime}\mid x,a)-\xi^{\top}(x,a)\beta_{\rho}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\right|\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d}.

Let

Vτ−1(k)​(x′)=maxa′∈𝒜⁡Q^τ−1(k)​(x′,a′),V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})=\max_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}}\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime},a^{\prime}),

and define the task-specific one-step Bellman coefficient

βτ(k)=βr(k)+γ​∫𝒳Vτ−1(k)​(x′)​βρ(k)​(x′)​d​x′.\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}=\beta_{r}^{(k)}+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{X}}V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\beta_{\rho}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\,dx^{\prime}. (\thechapter.A.24)

By the definition of fτ(k)f_{\tau}^{(k)},

fτ(k)​(x,a)=r(k)​(x,a)+γ​∫𝒳Vτ−1(k)​(x′)​ρ(k)​(x′∣x,a)​d​x′.f_{\tau}^{(k)}(x,a)=r^{(k)}(x,a)+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{X}}V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\rho^{(k)}(x^{\prime}\mid x,a)\,dx^{\prime}.

The uniform boundedness of Vτ−1(k)V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}, together with the sieve approximation bounds above, implies

supx,a,k|fτ(k)(x,a)−ξ⊤(x,a)βτ(k)|≲p−κ/d.\sup_{x,a,k}\left|f_{\tau}^{(k)}(x,a)-\xi^{\top}(x,a)\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}\right|\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d}. (\thechapter.A.25)

Let Zτ(k)∈ℝnk×qZ_{\tau}^{(k)}\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{k}\times q} be the design matrix whose rows are

ξ⊤​(Xi,t(k),Ai,t(k)),(i,t)∈Sτ(k).\xi^{\top}\left(X_{i,t}^{(k)},A_{i,t}^{(k)}\right),\qquad(i,t)\in S_{\tau}^{(k)}.

Let yτ(k)y_{\tau}^{(k)} collect the pseudo-responses Yi,t(k),τY_{i,t}^{(k),\tau}, and let eτ(k)e_{\tau}^{(k)} collect the corresponding regression noise terms. Define the sample sieve-approximation remainder by

rτ(k)=fτ(k)−Zτ(k)​βτ(k),r_{\tau}^{(k)}=f_{\tau}^{(k)}-Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\beta_{\tau}^{(k)},

where fτ(k)f_{\tau}^{(k)} on the right-hand side denotes the vector obtained by evaluating the regression function at the sample design points.

The task-specific regression representation is therefore

yτ(k)=Zτ(k)βτ(k)+rτ(k)+eτ(k),k=0,1,…,K,y_{\tau}^{(k)}=Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}+r_{\tau}^{(k)}+e_{\tau}^{(k)},\qquad k=0,1,\ldots,K, (\thechapter.A.26)

with

‖rτ(k)‖∞≲p−κ/d.\left\|r_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{\infty}\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d}. (\thechapter.A.27)

In this setting, the population Bellman coefficients βτ(k)\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}, population design matrices Σ(k)\Sigma^{(k)}, and associated discrepancy parameters may differ across tasks. The algebraic form of the joint regression problem remains unchanged. The remaining task is to characterize the target-source aggregate correction

δτ,Δ(0)=βτ(0)−∑k=1Kwk​βτ(k)\delta_{\tau,\Delta}^{(0)}=\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}-\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}

under heterogeneous rewards and transition kernels, after which the profiled joint-update analysis can be applied.

To quantify the primitive heterogeneity between the target task and the source tasks, define, for each k∈[K]k\in[K],

hk=‖βr(k)−βr(0)‖1+∫𝒳‖βρ(k)​(x′)−βρ(0)​(x′)‖1​d​x′,h_{k}=\left\|\beta_{r}^{(k)}-\beta_{r}^{(0)}\right\|_{1}+\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left\|\beta_{\rho}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})-\beta_{\rho}^{(0)}(x^{\prime})\right\|_{1}\,dx^{\prime},

and define the source-weighted primitive discrepancy

hw=∑k=1Kwk​hk.h_{\mathrm{w}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}h_{k}.

We also define the weighted discrepancy between the fitted task-specific coefficients at iteration τ\tau by

dτ=∑k=1Kwk​‖β^τ(k)−β^τ(0)‖2.d_{\tau}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(k)}-\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}.

The following lemma relates the target-source aggregate Bellman correction to the primitive task heterogeneity and the discrepancy inherited from the previous FQI iteration.

Lemma \thechapter.A.3 (Weighted Bellman discrepancy under transition heterogeneity).

Suppose the conditions of Theorem 5.2 hold, including the bounded-iterate condition and the transition-coefficient stability condition (4). Then, uniformly over τ=1,…,Υ\tau=1,\ldots,\Upsilon,

‖δτ,Δ(0)‖1≲hw+γ​dτ−1.\left\|\delta_{\tau,\Delta}^{(0)}\right\|_{1}\lesssim h_{\mathrm{w}}+\gamma d_{\tau-1}. (\thechapter.A.28)

Inequality (\thechapter.A.28) shows that the aggregate Bellman correction is controlled by the primitive weighted heterogeneity hwh_{\mathrm{w}}, together with the task discrepancy inherited from the preceding FQI iteration. To close this recursion, define

Eτ,0=‖β^τ(0)−βτ(0)‖2E_{\tau,0}=\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}

and

Eτ,s=∑k=1Kwk​‖β^τ(k)−βτ(k)‖2.E_{\tau,s}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(k)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}.

By adding and subtracting the corresponding population Bellman coefficients, we have

dτ\displaystyle d_{\tau} =∑k=1Kwk​‖β^τ(k)−β^τ(0)‖2\displaystyle=\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(k)}-\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2} (\thechapter.A.29)
≤Eτ,s+Eτ,0+∑k=1Kwk​‖βτ(k)−βτ(0)‖2\displaystyle\leq E_{\tau,s}+E_{\tau,0}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}
≲Eτ,s+Eτ,0+hw+γ​dτ−1,\displaystyle\lesssim E_{\tau,s}+E_{\tau,0}+h_{\mathrm{w}}+\gamma d_{\tau-1},

where the last inequality follows from the argument underlying Lemma \thechapter.A.3 and the inequality ‖u‖2≤‖u‖1\|u\|_{2}\leq\|u\|_{1}.

The target estimation error Eτ,0E_{\tau,0} is controlled by Lemma \thechapter.A.2. It remains to derive a corresponding reconstruction bound for the weighted source estimation error Eτ,sE_{\tau,s}. The next lemma provides this bound. The proofs of the auxiliary lemmas are collected after their statements.

Lemma \thechapter.A.4 (Weighted source-coefficient reconstruction).

Fix an iteration τ\tau, and condition on the previous fitted iterates. Define

gτ(k)=1nk(Zτ(k))⊤(eτ(k)+rτ(k)),k=0,1,…,K.g_{\tau}^{(k)}=\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{\top}\left(e_{\tau}^{(k)}+r_{\tau}^{(k)}\right),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots,K.

Under the conditions of Lemma 5.1, ℙ⁡(ℰΣ,τ)⟶1\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_{\Sigma,\tau})\longrightarrow 1. On this event,

Eτ,s≲∑k=1Kwk​‖gτ(k)‖2+1μ​(‖gτ(0)‖2+Eτ,0).E_{\tau,s}\lesssim\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|g_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}+\frac{1}{\mu}\left(\left\|g_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}+E_{\tau,0}\right). (\thechapter.A.30)

Moreover, uniformly over τ=1,…,Υ\tau=1,\ldots,\Upsilon,

‖gτ(k)‖2=Op(qnk+p−κ/d),k=0,1,…,K.\left\|g_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{k}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}\right),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots,K. (\thechapter.A.31)

Consequently, if

Eτ,0=Op​(rτ,0)E_{\tau,0}=O_{p}\left(r_{\tau,0}\right)

for some deterministic rate rτ,0r_{\tau,0}, then

Eτ,s=Op[K​qns+p−κ/d+1μ{qn0+p−κ/d+rτ,0}].E_{\tau,s}=O_{p}\left[\sqrt{\frac{Kq}{n_{s}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}+\frac{1}{\mu}\left\{\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{0}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}+r_{\tau,0}\right\}\right]. (\thechapter.A.32)

In particular, if K=O⁡(1)K=O(1), μ=ns/n0\mu=n_{s}/n_{0}, and ns≳n0n_{s}\gtrsim n_{0}, then

Eτ,s=Op[qns+p−κ/d+n0nsrτ,0].E_{\tau,s}=O_{p}\left[\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{s}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}+\frac{n_{0}}{n_{s}}r_{\tau,0}\right]. (\thechapter.A.33)

Lemma \thechapter.A.4 shows that the weighted source estimation error consists primarily of the source regression rate q/ns\sqrt{q/n_{s}}, while the effect of the target estimation error is attenuated by the factor 1/μ=n0/ns1/\mu=n_{0}/n_{s}. We first prove the two auxiliary lemmas and then combine their conclusions directly to close the finite-iteration recursion for dτd_{\tau}.

Proof of Lemma \thechapter.A.3.

Fix k∈[K]k\in[K]. By the definition of the task-specific Bellman coefficients in (\thechapter.A.24),

βτ(k)−βτ(0)=\displaystyle\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}={} βr(k)−βr(0)\displaystyle\beta_{r}^{(k)}-\beta_{r}^{(0)}
+γ∫𝒳Vτ−1(k)(x′)[βρ(k)(x′)−βρ(0)(x′)]dx′\displaystyle+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{X}}V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\left[\beta_{\rho}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})-\beta_{\rho}^{(0)}(x^{\prime})\right]\,dx^{\prime}
+γ∫𝒳[Vτ−1(k)(x′)−Vτ−1(0)(x′)]βρ(0)(x′)dx′.\displaystyle+\gamma\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left[V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})-V_{\tau-1}^{(0)}(x^{\prime})\right]\beta_{\rho}^{(0)}(x^{\prime})\,dx^{\prime}.

The first term is bounded directly by the reward component of hkh_{k}. For the second term, the uniform boundedness of the fitted value functions gives

‖∫𝒳Vτ−1(k)​(x′)​[βρ(k)​(x′)−βρ(0)​(x′)]​d​x′‖1\displaystyle\left\|\int_{\mathcal{X}}V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\left[\beta_{\rho}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})-\beta_{\rho}^{(0)}(x^{\prime})\right]\,dx^{\prime}\right\|_{1}
≤B​∫𝒳‖βρ(k)​(x′)−βρ(0)​(x′)‖1​d​x′.\displaystyle\leq B\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left\|\beta_{\rho}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})-\beta_{\rho}^{(0)}(x^{\prime})\right\|_{1}\,dx^{\prime}.

Consequently, the first two terms are bounded by a constant multiple of hkh_{k}.

For the third term, define

Gτ−1(k)​(x′)=Vτ−1(k)​(x′)−Vτ−1(0)​(x′).G_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})=V_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})-V_{\tau-1}^{(0)}(x^{\prime}).

The transition-coefficient stability condition implies

‖∫𝒳Gτ−1(k)​(x′)​βρ(0)​(x′)​d​x′‖1≤Cρ​∫𝒳|Gτ−1(k)​(x′)|​d​x′.\left\|\int_{\mathcal{X}}G_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\beta_{\rho}^{(0)}(x^{\prime})\,dx^{\prime}\right\|_{1}\leq C_{\rho}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left|G_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\right|\,dx^{\prime}.

Using

|maxa′⁡u⁡(a′)−maxa′⁡v⁡(a′)|≤maxa′⁡|u⁡(a′)−v⁡(a′)|,\left|\max_{a^{\prime}}u(a^{\prime})-\max_{a^{\prime}}v(a^{\prime})\right|\leq\max_{a^{\prime}}|u(a^{\prime})-v(a^{\prime})|,

we obtain

|Gτ−1(k)​(x′)|\displaystyle\left|G_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\right| ≤maxa′∈𝒜⁡|Q^τ−1(k)​(x′,a′)−Q^τ−1(0)​(x′,a′)|\displaystyle\leq\max_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}}\left|\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime},a^{\prime})-\widehat{Q}_{\tau-1}^{(0)}(x^{\prime},a^{\prime})\right|
=maxa′∈𝒜⁡|ξ⊤​(x′,a′)​(β^τ−1(k)−β^τ−1(0))|.\displaystyle=\max_{a^{\prime}\in\mathcal{A}}\left|\xi^{\top}(x^{\prime},a^{\prime})\left(\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}-\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(0)}\right)\right|.

By the second-moment condition on the sieve basis,

∫𝒳|Gτ−1(k)​(x′)|​d​x′≲‖β^τ−1(k)−β^τ−1(0)‖2.\displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left|G_{\tau-1}^{(k)}(x^{\prime})\right|\,dx^{\prime}\lesssim\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}-\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}.

Therefore,

‖βτ(k)−βτ(0)‖1≲hk+γ​‖β^τ−1(k)−β^τ−1(0)‖2.\left\|\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{1}\lesssim h_{k}+\gamma\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}-\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}.

Finally, since

δτ,Δ(0)=βτ(0)−∑k=1Kwk​βτ(k)=∑k=1Kwk​(βτ(0)−βτ(k)),\delta_{\tau,\Delta}^{(0)}=\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}-\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left(\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}\right),

the triangle inequality yields

‖δτ,Δ(0)‖1\displaystyle\left\|\delta_{\tau,\Delta}^{(0)}\right\|_{1} ≤∑k=1Kwk​‖βτ(0)−βτ(k)‖1\displaystyle\leq\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{1}
≲∑k=1Kwk​hk+γ​∑k=1Kwk​‖β^τ−1(k)−β^τ−1(0)‖2\displaystyle\lesssim\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}h_{k}+\gamma\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(k)}-\widehat{\beta}_{\tau-1}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}
=hw+γ​dτ−1.\displaystyle=h_{\mathrm{w}}+\gamma d_{\tau-1}.

This proves Lemma \thechapter.A.3. ∎

Proof of Lemma \thechapter.A.4.

For each task k=0,1,…,Kk=0,1,\ldots,K, define

uτ(k)=β^τ(k)−βτ(k).u_{\tau}^{(k)}=\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(k)}-\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}.

Recall that

gτ(k)=1nk​(Zτ(k))⊤​(eτ(k)+rτ(k)).g_{\tau}^{(k)}=\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{\top}\left(e_{\tau}^{(k)}+r_{\tau}^{(k)}\right).

Let

δ^τ=β^τ(0)−∑k=1Kwk​β^τ(k).\widehat{\delta}_{\tau}=\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}-\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(k)}.

By the first-order optimality conditions for the convex joint objective, there exists

z^τ∈∂‖δ^τ‖1\widehat{z}_{\tau}\in\partial\left\|\widehat{\delta}_{\tau}\right\|_{1}

such that the target and source KKT equations hold.

For the target coefficient, the KKT equation is

−1n0​(Zτ(0))⊤​(yτ(0)−Zτ(0)​β^τ(0))+λΔ​z^τ=0.-\frac{1}{n_{0}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(0)}\right)^{\top}\left(y_{\tau}^{(0)}-Z_{\tau}^{(0)}\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(0)}\right)+\lambda_{\Delta}\widehat{z}_{\tau}=0.

Using the regression representation

yτ(0)=Zτ(0)​βτ(0)+eτ(0)+rτ(0),y_{\tau}^{(0)}=Z_{\tau}^{(0)}\beta_{\tau}^{(0)}+e_{\tau}^{(0)}+r_{\tau}^{(0)},

we obtain

Σ^τ(0)​uτ(0)−gτ(0)+λΔ​z^τ=0.\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(0)}u_{\tau}^{(0)}-g_{\tau}^{(0)}+\lambda_{\Delta}\widehat{z}_{\tau}=0.

Equivalently,

λΔ​z^τ=gτ(0)−Σ^τ(0)​uτ(0).\lambda_{\Delta}\widehat{z}_{\tau}=g_{\tau}^{(0)}-\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(0)}u_{\tau}^{(0)}. (\thechapter.A.34)

For the coefficient of source task kk, the derivative of the fusion penalty contributes −λΔ​wk​z^τ-\lambda_{\Delta}w_{k}\widehat{z}_{\tau}. Hence the corresponding KKT equation is

−μ​wk​1nk​(Zτ(k))⊤​(yτ(k)−Zτ(k)​β^τ(k))−λΔ​wk​z^τ=0.-\mu w_{k}\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{\top}\left(y_{\tau}^{(k)}-Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\widehat{\beta}_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)-\lambda_{\Delta}w_{k}\widehat{z}_{\tau}=0.

Substituting

yτ(k)=Zτ(k)​βτ(k)+eτ(k)+rτ(k)y_{\tau}^{(k)}=Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\beta_{\tau}^{(k)}+e_{\tau}^{(k)}+r_{\tau}^{(k)}

gives

μ​wk​[Σ^τ(k)​uτ(k)−gτ(k)]−λΔ​wk​z^τ=0.\mu w_{k}\left[\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(k)}u_{\tau}^{(k)}-g_{\tau}^{(k)}\right]-\lambda_{\Delta}w_{k}\widehat{z}_{\tau}=0.

Since wk>0w_{k}>0,

Σ^τ(k)​uτ(k)=gτ(k)+λΔμ​z^τ.\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(k)}u_{\tau}^{(k)}=g_{\tau}^{(k)}+\frac{\lambda_{\Delta}}{\mu}\widehat{z}_{\tau}. (\thechapter.A.35)

Directly bounding z^τ\widehat{z}_{\tau} in ℓ2\ell_{2} would introduce an unnecessary factor q\sqrt{q}. Instead, substituting the target KKT identity (\thechapter.A.34) into (\thechapter.A.35) yields

Σ^τ(k)​uτ(k)=gτ(k)+1μ​[gτ(0)−Σ^τ(0)​uτ(0)].\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(k)}u_{\tau}^{(k)}=g_{\tau}^{(k)}+\frac{1}{\mu}\left[g_{\tau}^{(0)}-\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(0)}u_{\tau}^{(0)}\right].

Therefore,

uτ(k)=(Σ^τ(k))−1​{gτ(k)+1μ​[gτ(0)−Σ^τ(0)​uτ(0)]}.u_{\tau}^{(k)}=\left(\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{-1}\left\{g_{\tau}^{(k)}+\frac{1}{\mu}\left[g_{\tau}^{(0)}-\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(0)}u_{\tau}^{(0)}\right]\right\}. (\thechapter.A.36)

On ℰΣ,τ\mathcal{E}_{\Sigma,\tau},

‖(Σ^τ(k))−1‖op≤cG−1,‖Σ^τ(0)‖op≤CG.\left\|\left(\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq c_{\mathrm{G}}^{-1},\qquad\left\|\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq C_{\mathrm{G}}.

It follows from (\thechapter.A.36) that

‖uτ(k)‖2≲‖gτ(k)‖2+1μ​(‖gτ(0)‖2+‖uτ(0)‖2).\left\|u_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}\lesssim\left\|g_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}+\frac{1}{\mu}\left(\left\|g_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}+\left\|u_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}\right).

Multiplying by wkw_{k}, summing over k∈[K]k\in[K], and using ∑k=1Kwk=1\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}=1, we obtain

Eτ,s≲∑k=1Kwk​‖gτ(k)‖2+1μ​(‖gτ(0)‖2+Eτ,0).E_{\tau,s}\lesssim\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\left\|g_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}+\frac{1}{\mu}\left(\left\|g_{\tau}^{(0)}\right\|_{2}+E_{\tau,0}\right).

This proves (\thechapter.A.30).

It remains to establish the score bound (\thechapter.A.31). Decompose

gτ(k)=gτ,e(k)+gτ,r(k),g_{\tau}^{(k)}=g_{\tau,e}^{(k)}+g_{\tau,r}^{(k)},

where

gτ,e(k)=1nk​(Zτ(k))⊤​eτ(k)g_{\tau,e}^{(k)}=\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{\top}e_{\tau}^{(k)}

and

gτ,r(k)=1nk​(Zτ(k))⊤​rτ(k).g_{\tau,r}^{(k)}=\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{\top}r_{\tau}^{(k)}.

We first control the stochastic component. Conditional on ℱτ−1\mathcal{F}_{\tau-1}, the Bellman regression errors are mean-zero and have uniformly bounded conditional second moments. Moreover, the cross terms vanish by the martingale-difference property. Therefore,

𝔼⁡[‖gτ,e(k)‖22∣ℱτ−1]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|g_{\tau,e}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}^{2}\mid\mathcal{F}_{\tau-1}\right] =1nk2​∑(i,t)∈Sτ(k)𝔼⁡[(ei,t(k),τ)2​‖ξ⁡(Xi,t(k),Ai,t(k))‖22∣ℱτ−1]\displaystyle=\frac{1}{n_{k}^{2}}\sum_{(i,t)\in S_{\tau}^{(k)}}\mathbb{E}\left[\left(e_{i,t}^{(k),\tau}\right)^{2}\left\|\xi\left(X_{i,t}^{(k)},A_{i,t}^{(k)}\right)\right\|_{2}^{2}\mid\mathcal{F}_{\tau-1}\right]
≲qnk.\displaystyle\lesssim\frac{q}{n_{k}}.

Hence, by Markov’s inequality,

‖gτ,e(k)‖2=Op​(qnk).\left\|g_{\tau,e}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{k}}}\right). (\thechapter.A.37)

For the sieve-approximation component, using ∥rτ(k)∥∞≲p−κ/d\|r_{\tau}^{(k)}\|_{\infty}\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d}, we have

‖gτ,r(k)‖2\displaystyle\left\|g_{\tau,r}^{(k)}\right\|_{2} =‖1nk​(Zτ(k))⊤​rτ(k)‖2\displaystyle=\left\|\frac{1}{n_{k}}\left(Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)^{\top}r_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2} (\thechapter.A.38)
≤‖Zτ(k)‖opnk​‖rτ(k)‖2\displaystyle\leq\frac{\left\|Z_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n_{k}}\left\|r_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}
=λmax​(Σ^τ(k))​‖rτ(k)‖2nk\displaystyle=\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}\left(\widehat{\Sigma}_{\tau}^{(k)}\right)}\frac{\left\|r_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}}{\sqrt{n_{k}}}
≲p−κ/d.\displaystyle\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d}.

Combining (\thechapter.A.37) and (\thechapter.A.38) proves

‖gτ(k)‖2=Op(qnk+p−κ/d),\left\|g_{\tau}^{(k)}\right\|_{2}=O_{p}\left(\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{k}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}\right),

which is (\thechapter.A.31).

Next,

∑k=1Kwk​qnk\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{K}w_{k}\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{k}}} =qns​∑k=1Knk\displaystyle=\frac{\sqrt{q}}{n_{s}}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sqrt{n_{k}}
≤qns​K​∑k=1Knk\displaystyle\leq\frac{\sqrt{q}}{n_{s}}\sqrt{K\sum_{k=1}^{K}n_{k}}
=K​qns,\displaystyle=\sqrt{\frac{Kq}{n_{s}}},

where the inequality follows from Cauchy–Schwarz. Thus, whenever Eτ,0=Op​(rτ,0)E_{\tau,0}=O_{p}(r_{\tau,0}), (\thechapter.A.30) and (\thechapter.A.31) imply

Eτ,s=Op[K​qns+p−κ/d+1μ{qn0+p−κ/d+rτ,0}],E_{\tau,s}=O_{p}\left[\sqrt{\frac{Kq}{n_{s}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}+\frac{1}{\mu}\left\{\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{0}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}+r_{\tau,0}\right\}\right],

which proves (\thechapter.A.32).

Finally, suppose K=O⁡(1)K=O(1), μ=ns/n0\mu=n_{s}/n_{0}, and ns≳n0n_{s}\gtrsim n_{0}. Then

K​qns≍qns,\sqrt{\frac{Kq}{n_{s}}}\asymp\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{s}}},

and

1μ​qn0=n0ns​qn0=qns​n0ns≲qns.\frac{1}{\mu}\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{0}}}=\frac{n_{0}}{n_{s}}\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{0}}}=\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{s}}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{0}}{n_{s}}}\lesssim\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{s}}}.

Moreover,

1μp−κ/d≲p−κ/d.\frac{1}{\mu}p^{-\kappa/d}\lesssim p^{-\kappa/d}.

It follows that

Eτ,s=Op[qns+p−κ/d+n0nsrτ,0].E_{\tau,s}=O_{p}\left[\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{s}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}+\frac{n_{0}}{n_{s}}r_{\tau,0}\right].

This proves (\thechapter.A.33) and completes the proof. ∎

Define

Hτ=‖δτ,Δ(0)‖1H_{\tau}=\left\|\delta_{\tau,\Delta}^{(0)}\right\|_{1}

and, for x≥0x\geq 0, define

Δs​(x)=s​λ¯Δ∧x​λ¯Δ∧x.\Delta_{s}(x)=\sqrt{s}\,\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}\wedge\sqrt{x\overline{\lambda}_{\Delta}}\wedge x.

Also let

rn=qnall+qns+p−κ/d.r_{n}=\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{\mathrm{all}}}}+\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{s}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}.

The proof of Lemma \thechapter.A.2 is conditional on the preceding fitted iterates and uses hΔh_{\Delta} only through the iteration-specific bound

‖δτ,Δ(0)‖1≤hΔ.\left\|\delta_{\tau,\Delta}^{(0)}\right\|_{1}\leq h_{\Delta}.

Therefore, the same argument applied with HτH_{\tau} in place of hΔh_{\Delta} gives

Eτ,0=Op[qnall+p−κ/d+Δs(Hτ)].E_{\tau,0}=O_{p}\left[\sqrt{\frac{q}{n_{\mathrm{all}}}}+p^{-\kappa/d}+\Delta_{s}(H_{\tau})\right]. (\thechapter.A.39)

We now close the recursion by induction. Suppose that all tasks use a common initialization,

β^0(k)=β^0(0),k∈[K],\widehat{\beta}_{0}^{(k)}=\widehat{\beta}_{0}^{(0)},\qquad k\in[K],

so that

d0=0.d_{0}=0.

Suppose, for some τ≥1\tau\geq 1, that

Lemma \thechapter.A.3 then gives

The function Δs​(⋅)\Delta_{s}(\cdot) is nondecreasing and satisfies, up to absolute constants,

Δs​(x+y)≲Δs​(x)+y,x,y≥0.\Delta_{s}(x+y)\lesssim\Delta_{s}(x)+y,\qquad x,y\geq 0. (\thechapter.A.42)

Indeed, Δs​(x)≤x\Delta_{s}(x)\leq x, and its three-branch form is nondecreasing and subadditive. Consequently, (\thechapter.A.41) implies

Combining (\thechapter.A.39) and (\thechapter.A.43), we obtain

Since

it also follows that

Under K=O⁡(1)K=O(1), μ=ns/n0\mu=n_{s}/n_{0}, and ns≳n0n_{s}\gtrsim n_{0}, Lemma \thechapter.A.4 and (\thechapter.A.45) yield

=Op​(rn+hw).\displaystyle=O_{p}\left(r_{n}+h_{\mathrm{w}}\right).
